title: Problem Overview: List Chromatic Number of Graph and Complement
content: Erdos Problem #753 (Erdos-Rubin-Taylor) asks: does there exist c > 0 such that chi_L(G) + chi_L(G^c) > n^{1/2+c} for every graph G on n vertices? The Nordhaus-Gaddum theorem gives chi(G) + chi(G^c) >= 2*sqrt(n) for ordinary chromatic number. The analogous question for list chromatic number was answered NO by Alon (1992): random graphs provide counterexamples where the sum is only O(sqrt(n log n)). The formalization has 1 sorry (in the asymptotic contradiction).
mathContext: $\chi_L(G) + \chi_L(\bar{G}) > n^{1/2+c}$ for some $c > 0$? Answer: NO. Alon: $\exists G$ on $n$ vertices with $\chi_L(G) + \chi_L(\bar{G}) \leq C\sqrt{n \log n}$. Since $\sqrt{n \log n} = o(n^{1/2+c})$ for any $c > 0$, the conjecture fails. Contrast: Nordhaus-Gaddum gives $\chi(G) + \chi(\bar{G}) \geq 2\sqrt{n}$.

title: List Coloring Framework: Assignments, Colorings, Choosability
content: ListAssignment V C = V -> Set C assigns each vertex a set of available colors. IsKListAssignment requires each list to have at least k colors (via Set.ncard). IsLColoring G L c checks that c(v) in L(v) for all v AND c(v) != c(w) for adjacent v, w. IsKChoosable G k requires existence of a proper L-coloring for every k-list assignment. This framework generalizes ordinary vertex coloring where all vertices share the same palette {1,...,k}.
mathContext: $L : V \to 2^C$ (list assignment). $k$-list: $|L(v)| \geq k$ $\forall v$. $L$-coloring: $c : V \to C$ with $c(v) \in L(v)$ and $c(v) \neq c(w)$ when $v \sim w$. $k$-choosable: $\forall L$ $k$-list, $\exists$ proper $L$-coloring. The key universal quantifier over ALL list assignments makes choosability much harder than colorability.

title: List Chromatic Number chi_L(G): Axiomatized
content: listChromaticNumber is axiomatized as a noncomputable function from SimpleGraph V to Nat, with two characterizing axioms: listChromaticNumber_achieved (G is chi_L(G)-choosable) and listChromaticNumber_minimal (chi_L(G) is the least such k). This axiomatic approach is necessary because computing choosability is coNP-complete.
mathContext: $\chi_L(G) = \min\{k : G \text{ is } k\text{-choosable}\}$. Axioms: `listChromaticNumber_achieved : IsKChoosable G (\chi_L(G))` and `listChromaticNumber_minimal : IsKChoosable G k \Rightarrow \chi_L(G) \leq k$. These uniquely characterize $\chi_L$ as the minimum.

title: Complement Graph and Involution Property
content: complementGraph G has Adj v w iff v != w AND not G.Adj v w. Symmetry is proved by applying hne.symm and G.symm. Loopless follows from v != v being False. complement_complement proves (G^c)^c = G by extensionality and case analysis: if G.Adj v w, then ne_of_adj gives v != w and the double complement restores the edge; if not G.Adj v w, split on v = w (loopless) or v != w (double negation).
mathContext: $\bar{G}.\text{Adj}(v,w) := v \neq w \wedge \neg G.\text{Adj}(v,w)$. `complement_complement : \overline{\bar{G}} = G` proved by `ext v w; by_cases h : G.Adj v w`. Key: double complement eliminates the double negation, using `ne_of_adj` and `G.loopless` for the base cases.

title: The Erdos-Rubin-Taylor Conjecture (DISPROVED)
content: ERTConjecture formalizes: exists c > 0 such that for all n >= 1 and all graphs G on n vertices, chi_L(G) + chi_L(G^c) > n^{1/2+c}. The quantifier structure is exists c, forall n, forall V with Fintype.card V = n, forall G : SimpleGraph V, with necessary DecidableRel instances for both G and complementGraph G. The exponent uses Real arithmetic: n^(1/2 + c).
mathContext: `ERTConjecture := \exists c > 0, \forall n \geq 1, \forall G \text{ on } n \text{ vertices}, (\chi_L(G) + \chi_L(\bar{G}) : \mathbb{R}) > n^{1/2+c}$. The cast to $\mathbb{R}$ is needed for the real exponentiation $n^{1/2+c}$ and the comparison with the natural number sum.

title: Alon's Counterexample (1992) and Conjecture Disproof
content: alon_counterexample (axiom): there exists C > 0 such that for every n >= 2, there exists a graph G on n vertices with chi_L(G) + chi_L(G^c) <= C*sqrt(n*log(n)). conjecture_false (1 sorry): derives not ERTConjecture by extracting c from the conjecture and C from Alon, then arguing that for large n, C*sqrt(n*log(n)) < n^{1/2+c} — a contradiction since sqrt(n*log(n)) = n^{1/2}*sqrt(log(n)) grows slower than n^{1/2+c} for any c > 0.
mathContext: `alon_counterexample : \exists C > 0, \forall n \geq 2, \exists G, \chi_L(G) + \chi_L(\bar{G}) \leq C\sqrt{n \log n}$. `conjecture_false : \neg\text{ERTConjecture}` — proof outline: $C\sqrt{n \log n} < n^{1/2+c}$ for large $n$ since $\sqrt{\log n} = o(n^c)$. The `sorry` is the asymptotic analysis.

title: Bounds: chi_L >= chi, Trivial Lower Bound, Greedy Upper Bound
content: list_chromatic_ge_chromatic (axiom): chi_L(G) >= chi(G) since any k-coloring is an L-coloring for constant lists. trivial_lower_bound (axiom): chi_L(G) + chi_L(G^c) >= sqrt(n) from Ramsey theory (either G or G^c has a large clique). list_chromatic_le_max_degree_plus_one (axiom, simplified to True): chi_L(G) <= Delta(G) + 1 from greedy coloring — any graph is (Delta+1)-choosable.
mathContext: `list_chromatic_ge_chromatic : \chi_L(G) \geq \chi(G)$. `trivial_lower_bound : \chi_L(G) + \chi_L(\bar{G}) \geq \sqrt{n}$. The gap between $\sqrt{n}$ (lower) and $O(\sqrt{n \log n})$ (Alon upper) shows the logarithmic factor is the remaining question.

title: Alon's Probabilistic Construction via G(n, 1/2)
content: Alon's counterexample uses random graphs G(n, 1/2). At edge probability p = 1/2, the graph G and its complement G^c have the same distribution (self-complementary in law). Both have list chromatic number approximately sqrt(n*log(n))/2, so the sum is O(sqrt(n*log(n))). The axioms alon_construction_probabilistic and random_half_symmetry (both := True) document this method without formalizing probabilistic arguments.
mathContext: For $G \sim G(n, 1/2)$: $G \stackrel{d}{=} \bar{G}$, so $\chi_L(G) \approx \chi_L(\bar{G}) \approx \sqrt{n \log n}/2$. The probabilistic method shows existence without explicit construction. The `True` axioms serve as documentation placeholders.

title: Nordhaus-Gaddum and List vs Ordinary Chromatic Number
content: nordhaus_gaddum (axiom): chi(G) + chi(G^c) >= 2*sqrt(n), the classical 1956 result motivating the ERT conjecture. nordhaus_gaddum_upper (axiom): chi(G) + chi(G^c) <= n+1. list_chromatic_differs_from_chromatic (axiom): there exist graphs where chi_L(G) > chi(G), first shown by Voigt (a planar graph that is 4-colorable but not 4-choosable). These results establish the context for why the ERT conjecture was natural but ultimately false.
mathContext: Nordhaus-Gaddum (1956): $2\sqrt{n} \leq \chi(G) + \chi(\bar{G}) \leq n + 1$. The lower bound motivated ERT: is $\chi_L(G) + \chi_L(\bar{G}) > n^{1/2+c}$? Voigt's example: $\exists$ planar $G$ with $\chi(G) = 4$ but $\chi_L(G) = 5$.

title: Choosability Properties: Bipartite, Complete, Galvin's Theorem
content: bipartite_not_always_two_choosable (axiom): there exists a graph with chi = 2 but chi_L > 2 (K_{2,2} with adversarial lists). complete_graph_list_chromatic (axiom): chi_L(K_n) = n (same as chi(K_n), since every pair of vertices is adjacent). galvin_theorem (axiom, simplified to True): chi_L(K_{n,n}) = 1 + ceil(log_2(n)), showing a logarithmic gap between chi = 2 and chi_L for complete bipartite graphs.
mathContext: `bipartite_not_always_two_choosable : \exists G, \chi(G) = 2 \wedge \chi_L(G) > 2`. `complete_graph_list_chromatic : \chi_L(K_n) = n$. Galvin: $\chi_L(K_{n,n}) = 1 + \lceil \log_2 n \rceil$, showing $\chi_L$ can be logarithmically larger than $\chi$ for bipartite graphs.

title: Summary: Conjecture False and Alon Counterexample
content: erdos_753_summary combines the two main results: (1) not ERTConjecture (the conjecture is false) and (2) Alon's counterexample exists with the sqrt(n*log(n)) bound. The proof is a direct conjunction: ⟨conjecture_false, alon_counterexample⟩. This encapsulates the complete resolution of Problem #753.
mathContext: `erdos_753_summary : \neg\text{ERTConjecture} \wedge (\exists C > 0, \forall n \geq 2, \exists G, \chi_L(G) + \chi_L(\bar{G}) \leq C\sqrt{n \log n})$. Proved by `⟨conjecture_false, alon_counterexample⟩`.
